chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Zayd al-Shahham said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the will (al-wasiyyah), and he said: 'It is a right upon every Muslim.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: The will or testament, specifically referring to bequests made by a person before death.
key_terms.حَقٌّ: A right or obligation, indicating a binding legal or religious duty.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on making a will (wasiyyah) for every Muslim?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the *wasiyyah* (will) as a universal obligation for every Muslim, emphasizing its role in fulfilling rights beyond statutory inheritance. This ruling underscores the ethical imperative to allocate a portion of one's estate for charity or specific bequests, ensuring spiritual continuity and social responsibility. The statement reflects the Shia juristic view that while inheritance is fixed, the will serves as a flexible mechanism for fulfilling additional religious and social duties.
